statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5318(g)?
statutory.answer: Neutral: 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) suspicious activity reporting may be implicated, but the facts do not show whether a covered financial institution detected suspicious activity requiring a SAR or failed to report.
statutory.label: neutral
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) authorizes/mandates suspicious activity reporting by covered financial institutions (via Treasury regulations) when the institution detects a suspicious transaction relevant to possible violations of law or other specified suspicious criteria. Here, the fact pattern describes a business (a securities broker/dealer) with several large wire/ACH transactions and a high risk rating, but it does not identify (i) whether the actor is a covered financial institution subject to SAR rules under § 5318(g), (ii) whether any transaction was actually detected/known by the institution to be suspicious under applicable criteria (e.g., indicative of money laundering, BSA violations, or lacking lawful purpose), or (iii) whether a SAR was required and not filed (or was filed). Because the elements tied to § 5318(g) suspicious activity reporting—coverage, detection of suspicious activity, and reporting obligation/violation—are not established by the provided facts, applicability cannot be determined.
